subject.title: Suppress model fallback notices in rooms

question: Should fallback transition and recovery notices be suppressed by default in every group/channel room, or only on explicitly external/user-facing delivery surfaces?
rationale: Current documentation promises visible notices, while the canonical issue establishes a privacy problem on external recipients; source inspection cannot determine the intended permanent visibility boundary.

options.title: Suppress all room notices
options.body: Approve the PR's broad group/channel policy, but move suppression inside the notice-building path so lifecycle events remain emitted and require room-versus-DM proof.

options.title: Use a source-aware policy
options.body: Gate notices through an existing or new delivery-visibility policy that distinguishes external recipients from trusted operator rooms.

options.title: Keep current behavior
options.body: Retain visible notices everywhere and close this direction if operators are expected to manage routing-detail exposure through deployment design.

recommendation.title: Suppress all room notices
recommendation.body: Approve the PR's broad group/channel policy, but move suppression inside the notice-building path so lifecycle events remain emitted and require room-versus-DM proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They co-owned the original visibility design and specifically separated lifecycle events from user-message verbosity.
